name: hurdat-hadisst-data

Data + R/ code + data-raw/ + processed data/ folders, GPL-3.0, 2 stars (small, academic thesis project) but the underlying HURDAT2 source is NOAA-official and goes back to 1851 (Atlantic) / 1949 (E. Pacific).

name: hurdat2
what_it_holds: R package to read and analyze NOAA's HURDAT2 Atlantic/East-Pacific hurricane best-track dataset (storm name, date/time, lat/lon, max wind, pressure, category, for every storm since 1851/1949) directly from the NHC text feed into tidy tables.
why_useful: Landfall dates/locations/intensity for Q3/Q4 hurricane season (peak Aug-Oct, inside the pitch's forecast quarters) let the team build Florida/Caribbean/Gulf-market booking-disruption and cancellation dummies, and back-test past hurricane quarters against Inside-Airbnb-covered markets (New Orleans is in the 13-city panel).

name: NationalParkAnnualAttendance
what_it_holds: Group project (BYU Stat 386) combining the National Parks API with a scraper ('parks_scraper.ipynb', 'nationalparksdata' package) that builds an annual-attendance dataset; includes EDA/analysis notebooks and a Streamlit app. Exact file/row counts not visible from README alone.
why_useful: A working scrape method against NPS annual attendance figures (a public, non-Airbnb source) that could be re-run for a longer or more current series than what we hold; secondary/lower confidence versus national-parks-bi since data extent is unconfirmed from the README.

name: Time-Series-Forecasting-of-Visitation-in-Skiing-Resorts
what_it_holds: Datathon project (Australian inter-university) forecasting 2026 visitor-days for 9 Australian ski resorts using Exponential Smoothing, ARIMA and RNN models; also computes a skier-satisfaction index. Underlying visitation data for the 9 resorts is part of the repo (datathon-supplied).
why_useful: One of very few public repos with an actual ski-resort visitation time series (not just US, but a genuine destination-demand dataset with methods for forecasting a seasonal leisure-travel series); low direct relevance to ABNB's US/EU markets but the modeling approach (ARIMA/ETS/RNN on visitor-days) is transferable and the raw resort data is real.
